To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the correlation analysis does not always allow us to detect the presence of a relationship, especially in the case of a strong nonlinear relationship; 2) the use of a correlation matrix in the study of political preferences leads to the conclusion that there are no relationships, while in reality there are strong simple nonlinear relationships, which can lead to significant errors; 3) the use of the method of quantile distributions makes it possible to identify and study the nature of these simple nonlinear relationships.
the correlation analysis does not always allow to identify all important dependences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of frequent lack of linear correlations in the presence of simple nonlinear relations.
the study of simple nonlinear relations in a real situation.
the problem of type 1 errors in correlation analysis when a linear correlation is absent but there is a real strong simple nonlinear relation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the study of the political preferences of young Russians there are no linear correlations with correlation coefficients exceeding 0.6 (the "significant" correlation), but at the same time there are many strong non-linear correlations, which are not taken into account by supporters of the "significant" correlations.
the traditional correlation approach is not applicable for studying the political preferences of young Russians.
the traditional correlation analysis is useless in the study of political preferences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results obtained in the study of political preferences are not a single case, but a typical example of a phenomenon that is widespread in various fields of science.
the linear correlation coefficient is not a good indicator of the strength of the relation.
we have demonstrated the presence of strong simple nonlinear relations in the case of absence of linear relations and the presence of system errors in case of the linear relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the traditional correlation analysis is often misleading and the results of the analysis of the data obtained with its use should be treated with extreme caution.
there is often a simple non-linear relation that completely changes a picture of a phenomenon and that the correlation analysis gives a result that does not allow to see this dependence.
in the presence of simple non-linear relations between variables the correlation analysis may not show any significant linear correlations between variables, which is a common situation.
